markdown_excerpt: Moshi is built on top of Helium, a text LLM which we build from scratch (Section 3.2), relying on high-quality text data to provide strong reasoning abilities to the model. We also propose Inner Monologue (Section 3.4.4), a training and inference procedure in which we jointly model text and audio tokens. This allows the model to fully exploit the knowledge imparted from the text modality, while remaining a speech-to-speech system. To enable real-time dialogue, we also design Moshi as a multi-stream architecture from the get-go (Section 3.4.3): The model is able to both speak and listen to the user at the same time, and does not need to explicitly model speaker turns. In addition, to capture the input user audio and output Moshi's voice with high quality and in an efficient manner, we propose Mimi (Section 3.3), a neural audio codec combining semantic and acoustic information into a single tokenizer by using residual vector quantization and knowledge distillation.
